answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each identity to run inside a trusted-execution enclave emitting a timed cryptographic heartbeat. An honest agent sustains this pulse cheaply, but an attacker forging ten thousand identities must provision ten thousand enclaves, each costing hardware, power, and staked collateral that slashing destroys when its heartbeat stops. Reputation becomes an ember kept burning only by continuous honest work; impostors crowding one knoll of shared silicon are exposed by identical attestation keys and liquidated in one round.
